title: world_kickstart/1 — three ways this player's story could start, or the user's own opening grounded. The seat emits fiction only: no id, no coordinate, no tick, no number of any kind, anywhere.

identity.description: The player as chosen or written by the user, echoed as premise. When the user wrote their own words, author descriptor and name FROM those words — their words outrank yours. No traits, no disposition, no interior (B-4).

descriptor.description: How the room sees this stranger at first sight.

scenarios.description: Exactly three when offering; exactly one when grounding the user's own opening. Each names a real, already-populated place from the authored world.

label.description: The opening in a short line, the way a chapter is named — this renders as the option the user picks.

place.description: canonical_name of the place they walk into. It must be a place the world authored, and at least one member of the cast must already start there — a visitor never enters an empty room.

why.description: Why they are here, as premise — a situation, never a feeling.

stated.description: The arrival in the player's own first person. This becomes their single perception and the only thing they know.

recommended.description: At most one scenario carries this; the surface highlights it as the default. Omit entirely when grounding the user's own opening.

new_cast.description: People the chosen identity references who do not exist in the cast — 'Joe, son of Dalma and Harry' makes Dalma and Harry real. Same shape as the world's own cast; each starts_in must be a place the world authored. Emit ONLY people the identity itself references; empty or absent is the ordinary case.

descriptor.description: How a stranger sees this person before learning anything — 'a hooded figure by the bar'. This is what renders until the player earns the name, so it must stand alone as an introduction.

canonical_name.description: Their true name, and the join key other parts reference.

standing.description: What they do and where they sit in this world's order, in a phrase.

speech_manner.description: How they talk — clipped, formal, wheedling, flat. The cognition seats read this.

strength.description: A qualitative magnitude. The engine maps it to the number the schema forbids the seat from emitting.

manner.description: How that disposition shows in behaviour.

hiding.description: The one thing this person knows and does not say. It becomes a private perception only they hold — the planted secret the engine's own I-3 test hunts for leaks of.

malleability.description: A qualitative magnitude. The engine maps it to the number the schema forbids the seat from emitting.

starts_in.description: canonical_name of the place they are in when the player walks in.
